Comprehension Passage.main_question: Read the passage and answer the questions
Comprehension Passage.passage: Samina lived in a small village near a wide river. Every morning she carried a basket of fresh bread to the market. One day she found a tiny kitten shivering under a tree. The kitten was wet and hungry. Samina wrapped it in her scarf and shared a piece of bread with it. Then she walked to the market, holding the kitten gently. A kind shopkeeper gave her a bowl of warm milk. The kitten drank it quickly and purred happily. Samina smiled. She decided to keep the kitten and named it Moti. From that day, Moti waited at the door each morning and followed her to the market. The villagers loved to see the little kitten sitting beside the basket of bread, and Samina felt proud of her kindness.

questions.question: Where did Samina live?
questions.answer: She lived in a small village near a wide river.

points.text: States a small village
States near a wide river

accept: In a village beside a river
Near a river in a small village
scheme.common_error: Writing only the name Samina or the market

questions.question: What did Samina find under the tree?
questions.answer: She found a tiny, wet and hungry kitten shivering under the tree.

points.text: Names a kitten
Describes its condition (shivering, wet or hungry)

scheme.common_error: Saying she found bread or a scarf

questions.question: How did Samina keep the kitten warm?
questions.answer: She wrapped it in her scarf.

points.text: States she wrapped the kitten
States in her scarf

accept: She covered the kitten with her scarf
Used her scarf to wrap it
scheme.common_error: Saying she gave it milk

questions.question: Who gave the kitten warm milk?
questions.answer: A kind shopkeeper gave the kitten warm milk.

points.text: Names the shopkeeper
Gives a complete sentence answer

accept: A kind man in the market shop
scheme.common_error: Writing Samina as the answer

questions.question: Why do you think the villagers loved to see Moti beside the basket?
questions.answer: Moti was cute and the villagers admired Samina's kindness in caring for it.

points.text: Gives a sensible reason such as the kitten being cute or happy
Links the reason to Samina's kindness

accept: Because the kitten looked sweet and happy
Because they liked Samina's kind act
scheme.common_error: Repeating the sentence from the passage without a reason

questions.question: What part of speech is the word "gently"?

points.text: Names the correct part of speech

scheme.common_error: Calling it an adjective

questions.question: Change the sentence into the future tense: "Samina carried a basket of fresh bread to the market."
questions.answer: Samina will carry a basket of fresh bread to the market.

points.text: Correct future tense form with will and base verb

accept: Samina is going to carry a basket of fresh bread to the market.
scheme.common_error: Writing will carried

questions.question: Fill in the blank with a word from the passage: The kitten drank the warm milk ________ and purred happily.

points.text: Writes the correct word quickly

scheme.common_error: Writing quick

questions.question: Write True or False: Samina left the kitten under the tree.

points.text: Writes False

scheme.common_error: Writing True after missing that she took the kitten along

parts.instruction: Write the number of words asked for, copied exactly as they appear in the passage. Two extra words are allowed.

questions.question: Pick five nouns from the passage (the first three that are correct will be marked).

scheme.common_error: Changing the form of a word or choosing a verb

questions.question: Pick five verbs from the passage (the first three that are correct will be marked).

scheme.common_error: Writing the base form such as walk instead of walked

Punctuation.main_question: Rewrite the passage with correct capital letters and punctuation marks
Punctuation.question: pinky asked jojo what is your superpower jojo smiled and said it is forgiveness and it makes pinkys day feel light
Punctuation.answer: Pinky asked Jojo, "What is your superpower?" Jojo smiled and said, "It is forgiveness!" and it makes Pinky's day feel light.

points.text: Capital letters used correctly for names (Pinky, Jojo) and sentence starts
Full stops or sentence-ending marks used correctly
Question mark placed correctly after the question
Comma(s) placed correctly
Apostrophe placed correctly in Pinky's

accept: Use of quotation marks around spoken words, with or without them if the sentence is punctuated correctly
Exclamation mark or full stop after 'It is forgiveness'
scheme.common_error: Forgetting capital letters for names and omitting the apostrophe in Pinky's

Word Sentences.main_question: Write the meaning of each given word and use any five of the words in sentences of your own
Word Sentences.question: Write the meaning of each word. Then use any five words in sentences.
Word Sentences.answer:
invisible: cannot be seen - The air is invisible.
shrugs: raises and lowers shoulders to show you don't care or understand - Ali shrugs when he does not know the answer.
forgiveness: letting go of a grudge against someone - Forgiveness makes me feel light.
annoyance: feeling of being irritated or bothered - She showed her annoyance with a frown.
invent: to create something that never existed before - Scientists invent new machines.
baffled: being confused - The puzzle left Sara baffled.

points.text: Correct meanings shown for the words (1 mark each for five words)
Correct, meaningful sentences for five words (1 mark each)

accept: Meaning given in the child's own correct words
scheme.common_error: Writing a sentence that does not show the meaning of the word

Rhyming Words.main_question: Read the poem lines and write the four words that rhyme in pairs
Rhyming Words.question: Colours
Rhyming Words.passage:
My skin is kind of sort of brownish pinkish yellowish white.
My eyes are greyish blueish green,
But I'm told they look orange at night.
My hair is reddish blondish brown,
But it's silver when it's wet.
And all the colours I am inside
Have not been invented yet.

points.text: First rhyming pair white – night written
Second rhyming pair wet – yet written

accept: Words in either order within a pair
scheme.common_error: Pairing words by meaning or by the first letter rather than by the ending sound

Mind Map.answer: Five possible branches: colourful clothes, festivals, different cultures, languages, the colours of nature

points.text: Central topic written in the middle
Five branches drawn (1 mark for one branch, up to 4 marks across branches)

Application Writing.main_question: Write an application to your principal for sick leave
Application Writing.question: Write an application to your principal for sick leave.
Application Writing.answer: A formal application: To the Principal, school name, date, subject line, Respected Sir/Madam, reason of fever for two days, request for leave, thanks, Yours obediently, name and class.

points.text: Correct format: address to the principal, date and subject
Proper salutation and respectful opening
Reason for the illness clearly stated
Request for leave with the number of days
Correct closing and name
Correct spelling, capital letters and punctuation

accept: Application written with fever, cold or stomach ache as the reason
scheme.common_error: Using informal language or leaving out the subject line

Application Writing.main_question: Write a letter to your friend inviting them to a birthday party
Application Writing.question: Write a letter inviting your friend to your birthday party.
Application Writing.answer: An informal letter: address and date, Dear friend, a warm opening, invitation with date, time and place, mention of fun activities, request to come, closing as Your loving friend, name.

points.text: Correct format: address and date
Friendly salutation and opening
Party details given: date, time and place
Warm request to come and a friendly closing with name
Correct spelling, capital letters and punctuation

accept: Details of games, food or cake as the fun activities
scheme.common_error: Leaving out the date, time or place of the party

Paragraph Writing.main_question: Write a paragraph on any one of the following topics
Paragraph Writing.question: Write a paragraph on any one topic.
Paragraph Writing.answer: A paragraph of about 6 to 8 sentences with an opening sentence, details and a closing sentence. For My Super Hero: who the hero is, the superpower, how they help others, why the child admires them.

points.text: Clear opening sentence introducing the topic
Relevant details and ideas in order
Closing sentence
Correct grammar and tenses
Correct spelling, capital letters and punctuation

accept: Any one of the three topics
Simple present or simple past tense used consistently
scheme.common_error: Writing unrelated ideas or a single long sentence without punctuation

Story Writing.main_question: Write a story using the outline given below and give it a suitable title
Story Writing.question: A girl finds a lost kitten — She looks for its owner — Asks neighbours — Nobody knows — Feeds it milk — A boy comes crying — He is looking for his kitten — Kitten runs to him — Both are happy — Moral
Story Writing.answer: A story following all cues in order: a girl finds a lost kitten, searches for its owner, neighbours do not know, she feeds it, a boy arrives and the kitten runs to him, both are happy. Moral: Kindness and helping others bring happiness.

points.text: Story follows the outline cues in order
Past tense and correct sentences
Correct spelling and punctuation
A suitable moral written at the end

accept: Moral such as: Be kind to animals
Moral such as: Helping others makes us happy
scheme.common_error: Leaving out the moral or ignoring some cues

header.note_en: Note: This paper consists of THREE Sections. Section – A needs to be solved on the Question Paper. Sections B & C are to be solved on the Answer Sheet. Cutting, erasing and overwriting is not allowed.

slots.instruction_en: Read each question carefully and choose the correct option. Each question carries 1 mark.

grain.kind: one grammar or vocabulary point per item

slots.prompt_rule: Twenty four-option MCQs, one point each, covering: collective and proper nouns, articles, irregular plurals, antonyms, pronouns, syllables, adverbs, suffixes, tenses, homophones, compound words, degrees of adjectives, modals, apostrophe, spelling, anagrams, sentence types, quantifiers, adjectives. Never refer to an underline the paper cannot show; quote the word instead.

grain.kind: one-line transformation: rewrite as a simile, identify subject + verb + object, change the tense, simile or metaphor

slots.prompt_rule: Five one-line items, each ending with the direction in round brackets, e.g. "The baby is sleeping. (Change into simple past)". Cover similes/metaphors, S+V+O and simple present/past.

slots.instruction_en: Read the following passage and answer the questions given at the end.

parts_spec.label: iii.
parts_spec.instruction_en: Choose three nouns and three verbs from the given passage.

grain.kind: an unseen narrative passage of about 120 words; five literal or inference questions; four do-as-directed items tied to the passage; three nouns and three verbs

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `passage` = an unseen story of 120–160 words; `parts` = [{key:"questions", questions:[5]}, {key:"do_as_directed", questions:[4: a part of speech of a quoted word, a tense change, a fill-in from the passage, a true/false]}, {key:"pick", pick:{"Nouns":[5 nouns], "Verbs":[5 verbs]}}]. Every picked word is copied exactly as written in the passage, inflection included ("walked", never "walk"); two spares of each kind, the scheme keeps the first three that are in the passage. Never refer to an underlined, bold or italic word; quote the word instead (What part of speech is "quickly"?).

grain.kind: one or two sentences (about 25 words) with capitals, full stops, a question or exclamation mark, commas and an apostrophe removed

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `question` = the unpunctuated passage (lower case, no punctuation), `answer` = the punctuated passage. A points only, one per mark.

slots.instruction_en: Use any five of the following words in meaningful sentences.

grain.kind: six unit vocabulary words, any five used in sentences

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `words` = exactly six words from units 1–10; `answer` = one model sentence per word. 2 marks a word (meaning shown 1 + correct sentence 1).

slots.instruction_en: Write down FOUR rhyming words from the poem “{q}”

grain.kind: match four cue words to their rhymes in a 9–10 line poem from the book

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `question` = the title of a poem from units 1–10 exactly as in the book; `passage` = 6–10 of its lines exactly as printed in the book, holding at least two rhyming pairs; no `words` (the four rhyming words are the answer, so nothing on the paper may list them); `answer` = the four rhyming words as two pairs, each word copied from the passage (e.g. "white – night; wet – yet").

grain.kind: a textbook topic; the child draws a map with five branches

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `question` = a short topic from units 1–10 (2–4 words). The child draws the map; never refer to boxes or branches printed on the paper. `answer` = five possible branches.

grain.kind: a formal application OR an informal letter from FDE's closed lists

slots.prompt_rule: Two items: (a) "Write an application to your principal for …" with a topic from closed_lists.applications; (b) "Write a letter …" with a topic from closed_lists.informal_letters.

slots.instruction_en: Write a paragraph on any ONE of the following topics.

grain.kind: three paragraph topics from FDE's closed list; the child writes one

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `topics` = three different titles from closed_lists.paragraphs, exactly as listed.

slots.instruction_en: Develop a story with a moral from the given outline. Also suggest a suitable title.

grain.kind: an outline of 8–12 cues separated by dashes, ending with "Moral"

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `question` = the outline, 8–12 short cues separated by " — ", ending "— Moral". No title.

slots.instruction_en: Describe the picture with the help of the given word bank. Also suggest a suitable title.

grain.kind: a nine-word bank for an everyday scene (classroom, park, market)

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `question` = a one-line scene for the teacher (e.g. "children painting in an art lesson"), `words` = 8–10 words a child would use to describe that scene. The paper prints a frame and the word bank; the teacher adds any picture that fits. Never describe the picture to the child.
